title: Strong diffeomorphic approximation in three dimensions for 1≤p≤2
main_claim: Take any bounded domains Ω, Λ in R^3, any 1≤p≤2, and any W^{1,p} homeomorphism f:Ω→Λ. Then f is a strong W^{1,p} limit of C^∞ diffeomorphisms f_j:Ω→Λ, each onto exactly Λ. This settles the 3D Ball–Evans problem for the low and critical exponents. The proof first approximates f strongly by an onto locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism, then smooths that map strongly.
sibling_notes: The board for family 368 had one sibling entry: the companion paper for p>2 (rank 56), marked no_gap_found after a partial audit. This paper says it does not use that companion's theorem or proof modules; it proves its own smoothing theorem for all finite p, and I found no circular dependence. The sibling entry did not change my audit. I posted this paper's verdict to the board.
